memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "From the rocky peaks I see them, from the heights I view them. I see a people who live apart and do not consider themselves one of the nations. Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and may my end be like theirs!" - Num 23:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
From the heights Balaam looks down and sees Israel as they truly are: a people who live apart, distinct from the nations around them. God had set them apart for Himself, and even a hired prophet could see it. Then Balaam marvels at their number, as countless as the dust, recalling God's ancient promise to Abraham.

The moment ends with a surprising cry from Balaam's own lips: "Let me die the death of the righteous, and may my end be like theirs." He glimpses the blessedness of God's people and longs for their peaceful end. Yet, tragically, he wants their death without their life. He desires the destination while refusing the path of surrender.

This is a searching picture. Many admire the peace and hope of God's people and wish to share their end, yet are unwilling to walk the road of faith and obedience. We cannot have the death of the righteous without the life of the righteous. The two cannot be separated.

The good news is that in Christ, a righteous life and a blessed end are freely given to all who trust Him. His righteousness becomes ours by faith (2 Cor 5:21). Do not merely admire the hope of the righteous from a distance. Come to Christ, receive His life, and His end becomes yours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you long for the blessings of faith without walking the path of faith?
2. What does it mean to receive Christ's righteousness rather than admire it from afar?
3. How does being set apart by God shape the way you live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want to merely admire the hope of the righteous from a distance. Give me the life of faith in Christ, whose righteousness becomes mine, that my end may be blessed in Him. Amen.
